speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are here for an evaluation of systemic hypertension; to begin, how old are you and do you have a family history of high blood pressure or kidney disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Since this 5-year-old boy has no family history and no medications, we must investigate secondary causes for his hypertension. Does he have symptoms such as headaches, blurred vision, or complaints of snoring and sleep apnea?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Renal Artery Stenosis (likely Fibromuscular Dysplasia)

Thank you for that detail. The finding of hypertension isolated to the right upper extremity is highly suggestive of coarctation of the aorta or a proximal arterial obstruction. Can you confirm if there are any cold extremities, weak pulses in your legs, or a difference in blood pressure between your arms and legs? REQUEST IMAGES: Upper Extremity Doppler, Abdominal Ultrasound, Echocardiogram.
